findings.finding: _link_dry_run in composer.py calls resolve_hierarchy_link and checks only is_redundant and was_redirected — it does not check the 'error' key. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit Testing entry (and corresponding test case in `test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`) for cross-subtree same-type links — e.g. two tasks in different stories under the same epic — asserting that they ARE now promoted to story-level under the NCA rule (was_redirected=True), distinguishing this from the 1803 sibling case (same-parent, was_redirected=False).
evidence: SC3 test currently asserts: resolved_source='task-a1', resolved_target='task-b1', was_redirected=False for two tasks under different stories of the same epic.
Under the NCA rule, task-a1 and task-b1's NCA is epic-root; each escalates to its story ancestor → was_redirected=True, resolved story-a depends_on story-b.

Testing section names: 'Happy path: two direct children of the same parent link with no promotion', '1803 repro', 'jira-reb-1582 worked example', 'deep chain', 'ancestor rejection' — but NOT 'cross-story same-type tasks now get promoted'.
Scope says 'existing type-tier expectations are updated to the structural rule' but does not enumerate the expected new behavior.
findings.finding: The Testing section does not include a case for the behavioral inversion on same-type cross-subtree tickets — specifically, two tasks in different stories under the same epic that under the OLD rule linked unchanged (same tier 0) but under the NEW NCA rule WILL be promoted to story-level. This is the dominant behavioral change for existing callers and the scenario most likely to trigger unexpected redirections in the MCP link tool and reconciler apply path. The existing SC3 and SC5 test expectations (was_redirected=False for cross-story tasks) will flip, but this inversion is not enumerated as a named test case in the Testing section.
findings.location: Testing section; existing tests test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py SC3/SC5
scenarios: An implementer writing the SC3/SC5 tests might update them to the NCA expectation but omit the case where same-type cross-subtree links are promoted — leaving the new promotion path undertested.

A caller who relied on same-type task→task links passing through unchanged (old tier-0==tier-0 path) will now receive a redirect; if this isn't explicitly tested, the redirect JSON contract for this case goes unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing section: 'Behavioral inversion: two tasks in different stories under the same epic (`task-a1 depends_on task-b1` where both stories share `epic-root`) escalates to `story-a depends_on story-b` with `was_redirected=True`; verify the redirect JSON names the original and resolved pairs correctly.'
